baseline.name: Software and Systems Modeling
baseline.scope_notes: Foundations and applications of modeling languages and techniques for software, engineered/natural systems, and processes. Computational work includes formal modeling, transformations, scalable techniques, and rigorous experience analyses. Survey/overview and tool papers are also accepted. Tool papers must demonstrate community importance, lessons learned, availability as open-source or freemium software, and application in relevant scenarios.

route.conditions: Journal-specific publishing policy offers subscription publication without an APC; paid Open Choice is optional. Online color is free and print color can cost extra. baseline.audit_note: Independently read the journal-specific instructions and no-APC subscription policy. Retained needs_verification because submission/page costs are not explicitly settled; publisher-wide majority-no-charge wording cannot certify this title. Optional color, OA, and editing services do not themselves disqualify a free route. The official homepage and 2025-summary editorial disagree: homepage JIF 3.0, five-year JIF 2.9, downloads 523.7k versus editorial 3.2, 2.7 and 534505 respectively. Both identify 2025; no reconciliation was invented. Sources: https://link.springer.com/journal/10270 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10270-026-01361-1 . Review: removed 3 null-valued metric placeholder(s) (Journal Impact Factor, 5-year Journal Impact Factor, Downloads); no missing statistic is represented as a canonical observation. The conflicting figures remain documented above. Review directly checked scope, homepage, 24 February 2026 editorial, submission/AI conditions and the official tool-paper call (https://www.sosym.org/tool_paper/). The 466 submissions are not an established acceptance-rate denominator. First-decision timing remains undated. Tool/survey formats added; no conference-registration requirement is inferred for the regular journal route.

ai_policy.summary: Springer Nature explicitly permits supervised research assistance including exploratory data analysis and drafting explanatory summaries or literature reviews. These examples establish non-language research, analysis, and substantive drafting assistance; humans retain judgment, verify outputs, and take responsibility. The policy does not require permission to autonomously write an entire manuscript or make final interpretation.

disclosure.instructions: Describe AI research use in Methods; add an AI Use Declaration at the end directing readers to Methods and confirming accountability. Guidance requests tool versions, dates, prompts, and extent of contribution. Journal instructions say AI-assisted copy editing alone need not be declared, while current group guidance asks it be declared; follow the stricter disclosure.

restrictions: AI cannot be an author, replace scholarly judgment or write the entire manuscript; do not fabricate data or expose sensitive material to insecure tools.

policy_sources.note: Journal-specific submission guidelines give AI authorship and disclosure rules.
Explicitly permits analysis and drafting under oversight and sets end-of-paper declaration; current copy-edit declaration differs from journal instructions.
